**There are exactly two seasons on record — Fall 2023 and Winter 2024 — and nothing
athletic has been published since February 2024.** No win-loss series, no schedules and
no rosters exist. A record table would imply a continuity the data does not have.

> "The championship was clinched in a **54-23 victory at home over Carmel Christian**."

> "Coach Martin applauded Carmel for the team's 'incredible sportsmanship' during the
> season and in years past."

sections.preview: From "Congrats to Trinity's Fall Sports Teams", November 03, 2023, by Chris Miller. All verbatim: > "The 7th/8th Grade boys soccer team won the Queen City Conference title and tournament > championship." > "The 8th Grade volleyball team tied for first in the conference." > "Girls cross country was conference champion…
sections.text:
From "Congrats to Trinity's Fall Sports Teams", **November 03, 2023**, by Chris Miller.
All verbatim:

> "The **7th/8th Grade boys soccer team won the Queen City Conference title and tournament
> championship**."

> "The **8th Grade volleyball team tied for first** in the conference."

> "**Girls cross country was conference champion for the 4th year running, ranked first
> among independent schools in North Carolina, and had 7 runners named all-conference**."

> "**Boys cross country placed third** in the conference, had **3 runners in the top 15**
> in the championship, and had **1 runner named all-conference**."

> "We're also proud of our Wildcats on the **6th/7th Grade volleyball and soccer teams**,
> and the girls tennis team."

**The girls cross country line is the strongest single result Trinity publishes** — a
four-year conference title run plus a statewide independent-school ranking.

> ⚠️ Quote the school's own wording: "**ranked first among independent schools in North
> Carolina**", not "#1 among NC independent schools".

sections.preview: David Martin, Athletic Director and head basketball coach, verbatim: > "'For 20 daggum years, I have thought about this moment pretty much nonstop,' Martin > said." > "'I can't explain how much energy has gone into trying to win this tournament > championship over the last 20 years,' said Coach and Athletic Director…
sections.text:
**David Martin**, Athletic Director **and head basketball coach**, verbatim:

> "**'For 20 daggum years, I have thought about this moment pretty much nonstop,' Martin
> said.**"

> "'I can't explain how much energy has gone into trying to win this tournament
> championship over the last 20 years,' said Coach and Athletic Director David Martin."

> "**Martin has helmed the basketball team since its beginning in 2004 when he joined
> Trinity. By his count, some 250 students have played on the 8th Grade team in that
> time** and there have been many close brushes with the championship win."

> ⚠️ **"By his count, some 250 students"** — the hedge is the school's own. Carry it;
> do not present ~250 as a counted figure.

**Assistant Coach Jason Martin**, "another longtime Trinity staculty member."

A detail worth keeping for texture: the team presented the two coaches with **a clay
statue of themselves, made by team members in art class**, after the victory.

An earlier sweep recorded Grady Smith as coach of 8th-grade girls basketball, retired
June 2023. **This pass did not locate him in any athletics source.** He does appear in a
June 2023 staff-retirement post (threadid=2) among three retiring staff, but **no coaching
role is attributed to him there**.

**Status: not found — which is NOT the same as confirmed absent.** Do not ship the
coaching attribution, and do not record it as a verified null either.

sections.subtopic: The programme's stated philosophy — two quotable lines
sections.preview: Verbatim: > "Trinity Episcopal School's athletic department is all-inclusive, meaning we do not > make skill-based cuts. If a student wants to play one of the sports we offer then we > create that opportunity." > "Typically, 90% of the Middle School student body participates in our athletic > program either in the…
sections.text:
Verbatim:
> "Trinity Episcopal School's athletic department is all-inclusive, meaning **we do not
> make skill-based cuts**. If a student wants to play one of the sports we offer then we
> create that opportunity."

> "**Typically, 90% of the Middle School student body participates** in our athletic
> program either in the fall, winter, or spring. Most, in fact, play all three seasons.
> Our coaches enjoy preparing more experienced players for the next level, as well as
> introducing the game to interested student-athletes."

> ⚠️ **Quote the full clause.** "90% … participates" alone drops the seasonal qualifier
> ("either in the fall, winter, or spring"), which is what the figure actually measures.

**Motto:** "Play Hard, Play Smart, Play Together, and Have Fun"
**Athletic Director:** **David Martin** (dmartin@tescharlotte.org)

### ⚠️ Flag Football — a THREE-WAY source conflict

| Source | Flag football? |
|---|---|
| **2026-27 profile PDF** | **YES — listed in BOTH fall and spring** |
| **2025-26 profile PDF** | **NO — absent entirely** |
| **athletics.cfm (live page)** | **NO — not mentioned at all** |

Verbatim from the 26-27 profile:
> "Middle School Athletics: **Fall**- Girls' Volleyball, Co-ed Cross Country, Boys'
> Soccer, Girls' Tennis, **Flag Football** **Winter**- Boys' and Girls' Basketball
> **Spring**- Boys' Tennis, Co-ed Track & Field, Girls' Soccer, Co-ed Golf, **Flag
> Football**"

**Reading:** flag football appears to be **new for 2026-27**, and the athletics web page
has not been updated to include it.

> ⚠️ **Do NOT silently present this as 8 sports / 12 season-teams.** Report **7 sports /
> 10 season-teams** from the athletics page and footnote flag football as profile-only,
> new in 26-27, and not yet reflected on the athletics page.

sections.subtopic: ⚠️⚠️ CRITICAL NEGATIVE — Trinity is NOT in the GCMSAA
sections.preview: Trinity does not compete in the league the eight big Charlotte independents play in, and this is the most natural wrong assumption available. Independent corroboration, from Charlotte Country Day's own "2018-2019 Middle School Athletics Information Sheet" (PDF), verbatim: > "Greater Charlotte Middle School Athletics…
sections.text:
**Trinity does not compete in the league the eight big Charlotte independents play in**,
and this is the most natural wrong assumption available.

**Independent corroboration**, from Charlotte Country Day's own
"2018-2019 Middle School Athletics Information Sheet" (PDF), verbatim:

> "**Greater Charlotte Middle School Athletics Association:** All teams participate in
> the GCMSAA, which is a conference that brings together schools with a like-minded
> approach to middle school athletics. **Schools include: Cannon, Charlotte Christian,
> Charlotte Country Day, Charlotte Latin, Covenant Day, Holy Trinity, Lake Norman
> Charter, and Providence Day.** Teams will occasionally compete against schools outside
> this conference grouping to ensure a more complete schedule."

**8 of 8 members named. Trinity Episcopal is absent.**

And the positive side of the same fact: **Trinity competes in the Queen City Conference
(QCC)**, named twice in its own blog.

> **Never describe Trinity as competing against the peer schools already in this app.**

Two caveats carried honestly: the Country Day sheet is **2018-19**, so it establishes the
GCMSAA roster historically rather than for 2026-27; and it notes teams "occasionally
compete against schools outside this conference grouping", so an isolated fixture against
a peer is not impossible. Neither weakens the standing rule.

sections.subtopic: ✅ Confirmed present — the campus and its gymnasium
sections.preview: Corroborated firsthand from the architect's own project page (https://www.fmkarchitects.com/work/community/trinity-episcopal-school): - 106,500 sq ft on a 4.5-acre site - First Ward neighborhood, Charlotte NC - Phase I: classrooms, administrative offices, kitchen/cafeteria, primary infrastructure - Phase II: the…
sections.text:
Corroborated firsthand from the architect's own project page
(https://www.fmkarchitects.com/work/community/trinity-episcopal-school):

- **106,500 sq ft** on a **4.5-acre** site
- **First Ward neighborhood, Charlotte NC**
- **Phase I:** classrooms, administrative offices, kitchen/cafeteria, primary infrastructure
- **Phase II: the gymnasium**
- **Phase III:** chapel, library, large commons area
- Design constraints noted: the constrained land size, a landmark role for the
 "refurbished 9th Street corridor", and I-277 traffic noise

> ⚠️ **"106,500 sq ft" is copied char-for-char and must never be converted to m².**
> The unit-conversion allowlist was deleted 2026-08-24; a figure is copied as published,
> units included.

**This is the only athletics facility fact available**, and per the plan it belongs folded
into a sibling card rather than a facilities card of its own — there is nothing else to
put beside it.
